selected_authority_model.name: H1 advisory + framework-level C10 barrier
selected_authority_model.description: Two complementary mechanisms close the live defect at the framework seam: (a) H1 advisory in command_status returns `notification: "pending"` for notify-owned active jobs with waitMs>0, suppressing Path B resolveObligation. (b) Framework-level barrier at the C10 completion-commit seam consults `BackgroundNotifyCoordinator.hasActiveNotify(jobId)` (HOLD when marker alive) and `BackgroundNotifyCoordinator.wasWakeDelivered(jobId)` (SUPPRESS when wake delivered to pendingPrompts — wake-driven turn owns completion). The barrier is enforced at the `setTurnPhase("completed", ...)` call, NOT at the tool surface — the model CANNOT bypass it.

selected_authority_model.rationale: The H1 advisory is a comment-only convention the model MAY ignore — not load-bearing. The framework-level C10 barrier enforces the invariant at the lifecycle seam (`setTurnPhase("completed", ...)`) where the originating turn's `submit_and_exit` is committed. The barrier consults the per-job wake-delivered probe and SUPPRESSES the originating completion when the wake was delivered (the wake-driven turn owns terminal completion). Conservation: R4 (non-blocking read) + R5 (non-notify) + R6 (multi-job) all preserved.

halts.HALT_WAKE_DELIVERY_ACK_PROMOTED: CLOSED_BY_BOUNDED_CORRECTION_ROUND_3 (HALT_WAKE_DELIVERY_ACK_PROMOTED: the new authoritative fact is not actually authoritative — the prior ROUND 2 conflated wake-dispatch REQUESTED with wake DELIVERED at the moment of synchronous callback invocation. The production transport at SdkController.ts:738 is fire-and-forget `void active.sdkHost.send(...).catch(...)`; the coordinator had no ack signal so it marked the job as 'delivered' at callback invocation, not at the moment the wake actually landed. If the async send later rejected, the originating turn had already been SUPPRESSED and NO wake-driven turn would ever fire — semantic terminal completion count dropped to 0 (the opposite cardinality failure). ROUND 3 split the tracker into the explicit three-state contract: REQUESTED (set synchronously at callback invocation) / DELIVERED (set after async ack resolves with 'delivered') / FAILED (set after async ack resolves with 'rejected' or 'session_gone'). The C10 barrier consults all three states. Case 4 (wasWakeDispatchFailed) ALLOWS the originating turn's completion so semantic count for J is exactly 1 even when the wake is LOST. Case 2 (wasWakeDispatchRequested && !delivered && !failed) HOLDS the barrier while the ack is in flight (instead of incorrectly SUPPRESSING as ROUND 2 did). Production transport at SdkController.ts:738 changed from fire-and-forget to a real Promise<{ kind: 'delivered' | 'rejected' | 'session_gone' }> that awaits the underlying sdkHost.send and forwards the ack outcome to the coordinator. BNCA-FRAMEWORK-DISPATCH-FAILED-01 (3 tests) proves: case 4 (dispatch-FAILED) ALLOWS, case 2 (dispatch-REQUESTED) HOLDS, case 3 (dispatch-DELIVERED) SUPPRESSES. BNCA-FRAMEWORK-DISPATCH-FAILED-ABLATION-01 (4 tests) proves the ROUND 3 fix is load-bearing: fix ON holds during ack-pending and allows after ack-failed; fix OFF (wasWakeDispatchFailed probe unwired) does not hold — the originator commits immediately, which is exactly the silent defect ROUND 2 introduced.

halt_history.raised_at_round: factory expert (twenty-ninth reviewer; this ACT update)
halt_history.raised_observation: The framework-level C10 direction is the correct seam (ROUND 2 was right in principle). It fixes the previous model-dependence problem conceptually. But the new authoritative fact `wakeDeliveredJobIds means wake successfully enqueued into PendingPromptsController` is NOT actually authoritative. The production transport at SdkController.ts:738 is fire-and-forget `void active.sdkHost.send(...).catch(...)`. The coordinator marks the job as settled/delivered at its own `enqueueTerminalWake(...)` seam; that seam does not provide evidence that the asynchronous send has actually landed in PendingPromptsController. If the async send later fails / session disappears / enqueue rejects, no wake-driven turn runs, and the semantic terminal completion count for J drops to 0. Separately: ACT-owned evidence cannot simultaneously say `Errors 1` and `all passing` — re-run or explicitly classify the diagnostic against a proven baseline.
halt_history.required_repair: One bounded correction. (a) Make the state names and authority reflect an acknowledged boundary: dispatch-requested ≠ delivery-acknowledged. Either make `enqueueTerminalWake` await/return a real acknowledgment that the pending prompt was accepted, or retain the fire-and-forget transport but keep the originating completion HOLD until some existing production seam proves the wake landed. A failed delivery must settle toward a path that can still commit the originating completion rather than suppressing it forever. (b) Add the missing discriminator: wake dispatch requested → transport fails before PendingPrompts acceptance → originating completion is NOT lost → semantic completion count == 1. (c) Re-run a clean executable gate (no `Errors 1` artifacts) so evidence is honest.
halt_history.closed_observation: ROUND 3 changes the production transport at SdkController.ts:738 from fire-and-forget to a real Promise<{ kind: 'delivered' | 'rejected' | 'session_gone' }>. The BackgroundNotifyCoordinator now tracks THREE states explicitly: wakeDispatchRequestedJobIds (set synchronously at callback invocation), wakeDeliveredJobIds (set when host calls markWakeDelivered after async ack resolves with 'delivered'), wakeDispatchFailedJobIds (set when host calls markWakeDispatchFailed after async ack resolves with 'rejected' / 'session_gone'). The C10 barrier consults FIVE per-job cases (was THREE before): (1) hasActiveNotify → HOLD, (2) wasWakeDispatchRequested && !delivered && !failed → HOLD (was wrongly SUPPRESSED in ROUND 2), (3) wasWakeDelivered → SUPPRESS, (4) wasWakeDispatchFailed → ALLOW (closes the zero-completion failure mode), (5) isWakeAuthoritySettled (via discard) → ALLOW. New tests: BNCA-FRAMEWORK-DISPATCH-FAILED-01 (3 tests) — case 4 ALLOWS, case 2 HOLDS, case 3 SUPPRESSES; BNCA-FRAMEWORK-DISPATCH-FAILED-ABLATION-01 (4 tests) — fix ON holds during ack-pending and allows after ack-failed; fix OFF bypasses case-2 HOLD and the case-4 ALLOW gate (which is what ROUND 2 produced — the silent defect). Clean executable gate: 67 tests pass (20 BNCA + 47 conservation), 0 errors / 0 unhandled rejections (the HostProvider telemetry mock added to TQCB01 eliminates the unhandled-rejection noise artifact from the prior run).
